title: Parables of Jesus IQ
subtitle: The lost sheep, the prodigal son, the sower. How well do you know the stories Jesus told?

questions.text: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, who passed by the wounded man before the Samaritan stopped to help?

options.explanation: In Luke 10:31-32 both a priest and a Levite saw the man and passed by on the other side.

options.text: A soldier and a tax collector
options.explanation: No soldier or tax collector appears in this parable. It was a priest and a Levite.
Fishermen are not part of this story. The ones who passed by were a priest and a Levite.
Though Jesus told the parable to a lawyer, the men who walked past were a priest and a Levite.

questions.text: In the parable of the prodigal son, how did the father respond when his lost son came home?

options.explanation: The father did the opposite. He welcomed his son with open arms.

options.text: He ran to him and threw a feast
options.explanation: In Luke 15:20-23 the father ran to his son, kissed him, and killed the fatted calf to celebrate.

options.text: He made him work off his debt
options.explanation: The son offered to be a servant, but the father restored him as a son instead.

options.text: He sent him to live with the servants
options.explanation: The father put a robe and ring on him and treated him as a son, not a servant.

questions.text: In the parable of the sower, what happened to the seed that fell on rocky ground?

options.text: The birds ate it at once
options.explanation: The birds ate the seed that fell by the wayside, not the seed on rocky ground.

options.text: It sprang up fast but withered when the sun came up
options.explanation: In Matthew 13:5-6 the seed on stony ground sprang up quickly but had no root, so the sun scorched it.
The thorns choked the seed that fell among them, not the seed on rocky ground.
Only the seed on good ground produced a great harvest.

questions.text: In the parable of the lost sheep, how many sheep did the shepherd leave to find the one that wandered off?

options.explanation: In Luke 15:4 the shepherd leaves the ninety and nine to go after the one that is lost.
The number in the parable is ninety-nine, not forty-nine.
Twelve points to the disciples, not the flock in this parable.
Seventy were sent out in another passage, but the flock here numbered ninety-nine.

questions.text: In the parable of the mustard seed, what does the tiny seed grow into?

options.explanation: Wheat belongs to a different parable. The mustard seed becomes a tree.

options.text: A great tree where birds rest in its branches
options.explanation: In Matthew 13:32 the smallest of seeds grows into a tree, and the birds come and lodge in its branches.
The vine is its own picture in John 15. Here the mustard seed grows into a tree.
Thorns appear in the parable of the sower, not here. The mustard seed becomes a tree.

questions.text: In the parable of the ten virgins, what did the five wise ones bring that the foolish ones forgot?

options.explanation: In Matthew 25:4 the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps, but the foolish did not.
The parable is about readiness, not gifts. The wise brought extra oil.
A wedding garment appears in a different parable. Here the key item was oil.
No bread is mentioned. The wise virgins brought extra oil for their lamps.

questions.text: In the parable of the talents, what did the servant who received one talent do with it?

options.explanation: The servants with five and two talents doubled theirs. The one-talent servant did not.

options.text: He gave it to the poor
options.explanation: The parable does not say he gave it away. He hid it.

options.text: He buried it in the ground
options.explanation: In Matthew 25:18 the servant dug in the earth and hid his lord's money.
No thieves took it. He buried it himself out of fear.

questions.text: What is the main point Jesus made with the parable of the unforgiving servant?

options.explanation: This parable is about mercy, not money management.

options.text: Forgive others as you have been forgiven
options.explanation: In Matthew 18:32-35 the servant was forgiven a huge debt but refused to forgive a small one, and Jesus warned us to forgive from the heart.
The parable is not about working hard. It is about showing mercy.
The lesson is about forgiveness toward others, not simply obeying authority.

questions.text: In the parable of the wheat and the tares, what did the owner tell his servants to do with the weeds growing among the wheat?

options.explanation: The owner said not to pull them yet, in case the wheat came up with them.

options.text: Let both grow together until the harvest
options.explanation: In Matthew 13:30 the owner says to let both grow together, then separate them at harvest time.
Only the tares were to be burned, and only at the harvest, not the whole field.

options.text: Replant the field with new seed
options.explanation: There was no replanting. The owner let the wheat and tares grow until harvest.

questions.text: In the parable of the pearl of great price, what did the merchant do to obtain the one valuable pearl?

options.text: He sold all that he had to buy it
options.explanation: In Matthew 13:46 the merchant found one pearl of great price and sold all he had to buy it.

options.text: He traded a field for it
options.explanation: A field shows up in the parable just before this one. The merchant sold everything for the pearl.

options.text: He found it for free in a net
options.explanation: The net belongs to a different parable. The merchant paid everything for the pearl.

options.text: He borrowed money to buy it
options.explanation: He did not borrow. He sold all he owned to gain the pearl.

questions.text: Why did Jesus often teach the crowds using parables?

options.text: Because He could not speak plainly
options.explanation: Jesus could speak plainly. He chose parables on purpose to reveal truth to those ready to hear.

options.text: To teach spiritual truths through everyday stories
options.explanation: Jesus used familiar pictures like seeds, sheep, and coins to open up the truths of the kingdom (Matthew 13:34-35).
His parables were not entertainment for officials. They taught the truths of God's kingdom.
No law required parables. Jesus used them as a way to teach deep truth simply.

scoring.perfectMessage: Perfect. You know the stories Jesus told by heart.

gradeBands.label: New Listener
gradeBands.message: The parables reward a slow, careful read. Dive back in.

gradeBands.label: Following Along
gradeBands.message: You know the famous ones. Keep exploring the rest.

gradeBands.label: Close Reader
gradeBands.message: You know these stories well. Well done.

gradeBands.label: Storyteller
gradeBands.message: You could retell every one of these parables yourself.
